findings.title: Image conversion is invoked with the same input and output path
findings.body: `OptimizedImage.downsize` is called with `tempfile.path` for both `from` and `to`. The generated `convert`/`gifsicle` command is therefore asked to overwrite its input while reading it; these tools can reject identical input/output files or truncate/corrupt the source depending on format/version. As a result, oversized uploads will commonly fail to be reduced (and may leave an invalid tempfile) before `Upload.create_for` runs. Write to a separate tempfile, verify conversion succeeded, then replace the original only after success.

findings.title: The new downsize overload removes the existing five-argument API
findings.body: Ruby does not support method overloading. Defining `downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` here replaces the preceding `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` definition entirely. Any existing caller using the previously supported width/height form now receives `ArgumentError: wrong number of arguments`, breaking thumbnail/image-processing callers outside this diff. Preserve both calling conventions with a single variadic method or use a differently named helper.

findings.title: Client-side upload validation now ignores configured per-type limits
findings.body: The upload validator formerly used `max_image_size_kb` or `max_attachment_size_kb` according to `type`; it now accepts every file up to a hard-coded 10 MB. This means attachments above a site's configured attachment limit are sent only to be rejected by the server, while sites configured to permit files larger than 10 MB are rejected in the browser. The automatic-reduction exception should be limited to images and the configured attachment limit must remain enforced.

findings.title: 413 errors report a hard-coded limit rather than the site limit
findings.body: The error shown for a server-side 413 always says 10 MB, even when the server/proxy rejected the upload because the site's configured image or attachment limit is different. This gives users an incorrect actionable limit and is inconsistent with the server configuration.

findings.title: The new destructive upload transformation has no coverage
findings.body: There are no tests for the new upload-time resize path, including successful reduction below `max_image_size_kb`, conversion failure handling, animated GIF handling, and preserving normal attachment limits. This is particularly important because the implementation mutates the uploaded tempfile before persistence and because the current same-path conversion call can fail silently before the upload validation response.
